content.title: Successful published book detail page shows bibliographic details, cover image, and a linked publishing package

check.operand: text matching `ISBN: <isbn-13>` where `<isbn-13>` is a valid ISBN-13

content.test_md_blob:
# Successful published book detail page shows bibliographic details, cover image, and a linked publishing package

> Prove that a valid published-book detail page renders the promised credibility details, cover image, published-via package statement, and package link on the successful detail-page outcome.

## Step 1

Open {{home_page_url}} in the browser and use the header search for `The Iron Court` to reach the detail page for `The Iron Court` by `Branwen Oduya`.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-125, ac-128, ac-129, ac-130, ac-131, ac-132, ac-133, ac-134, ac-135, ac-136

On the `The Iron Court` detail page, inspect the bibliographic content area and the cover area, then assert the page shows the title `The Iron Court`, the author `by Branwen Oduya`, a genre, `Rating: <n>`, a format, an `ISBN:` value formatted as a valid ISBN-13, `Published <Month YYYY>`, a blurb, a cover image, and the statement `Published via our <package name> package.` with the package name rendered as a link.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-126

From the `Published via our <package name> package.` statement on the same detail page, open the linked package name, then assert the destination page shows package detail content including its code, tagline, price, and `Turnaround: <n> business days`.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - objective: Open {{home_page_url}} in the browser and use the header search for `The Iron Court` to reach the detail page for `The Iron Court` by `Branwen Oduya`.
    step: 1
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: presence
      operand: 'text matching `ISBN: <isbn-13>` where `<isbn-13>` is a valid ISBN-13'
      operator: exists
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-133
    objective: 'On the `The Iron Court` detail page, inspect the bibliographic content area and the cover area, then assert the page shows the title `The Iron Court`, the author `by Branwen Oduya`, a genre, `Rating: <n>`, a format, an `ISBN:` value formatted as a valid ISBN-13, `Published <Month YYYY>`, a blurb, a cover image, and the statement `Published via our <package name> package.` with the package name rendered as a link.'
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-125
      - ac-128
      - ac-129
      - ac-130
      - ac-131
      - ac-132
      - ac-133
      - ac-134
      - ac-135
      - ac-136
  - objective: 'From the `Published via our <package name> package.` statement on the same detail page, open the linked package name, then assert the destination page shows package detail content including its code, tagline, price, and `Turnaround: <n> business days`.'
    step: 3
    verifies:
      - ac-126
scenario: Open an existing published book detail page and inspect its bibliographic details, cover image, and package link
title: Successful published book detail page shows bibliographic details, cover image, and a linked publishing package

# Publish-your-book CTA on a published book detail page routes to the publishing packages page

> Prove that the book-detail-page conversion CTA routes the reader from a valid book page into the publishing packages page.

## Step 1

Open {{home_page_url}} in the browser and use the header search for `The Iron Court` to reach the detail page for `The Iron Court` by `Branwen Oduya`.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-127

On the `The Iron Court` detail page, activate the `Publish your book like this one` call to action, then assert the browser URL is `/publish`.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - objective: Open {{home_page_url}} in the browser and use the header search for `The Iron Court` to reach the detail page for `The Iron Court` by `Branwen Oduya`.
    step: 1
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: propagation
      operand: /publish
      operator: equals
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-127
    objective: On the `The Iron Court` detail page, activate the `Publish your book like this one` call to action, then assert the browser URL is `/publish`.
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-127
scenario: Use the publish-your-book CTA on a published book detail page to reach /publish
title: Publish-your-book CTA on a published book detail page routes to the publishing packages page

# Missing published book detail request returns HTTP 404

> Prove that a missing published-book detail request returns a 404 rather than rendering a misleading detail page.

## Step 1 @verifies ac-137

Open {{home_page_url}} in the browser, then request {{nonexistent_book_detail_url}} in the same tab, then assert the main document response status is HTTP 404.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: absolute
      operand: HTTP 404
      operator: equals
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-137
    objective: Open {{home_page_url}} in the browser, then request {{nonexistent_book_detail_url}} in the same tab, then assert the main document response status is HTTP 404.
    step: 1
    verifies:
      - ac-137
scenario: Request a published book detail page that does not exist and receive a 404
title: Missing published book detail request returns HTTP 404

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Kept first because this pair proves the main successful detail-page journey and covers most of the public credibility promises plus the package handoff.
[value_score] Kept second because this pair proves the explicit conversion route from a book page back into publishing.
[value_score] Kept third because the negative missing-book 404 outcome is explicitly promised and should be exercised even though it covers fewer criteria than the successful path.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the written check narrowly proves the valid ISBN-13 promise from **ac-133**, while the step-level asserts prove the other presence criteria and the package-link navigation. Technique fit: a successful rendered-page inspection is the correct happy-path technique here. Negative coverage is not missing because **sc-28** covers the absent-resource outcome. Over-broad asserts were avoided by limiting the package-destination proof to package-detail content the source explicitly states.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check exactly proves the `/publish` destination promised by **ac-127**. Technique fit: direct happy-path navigation is appropriate for a CTA routing promise. Negative coverage is not missing inside this test because the use-case already carries a separate negative scenario for missing resources. Over-broad asserts were avoided by checking only the CTA destination, not unrelated page content.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the check exactly proves the HTTP 404 outcome promised by **ac-137**. Technique fit: a direct negative request is the right way to exercise missing-resource behavior. The remaining weakness is not oracle breadth but missing grounded input, so I recorded the concrete URL as an incomplete gap instead of inventing one.
